text: The following question stood in the name of  Ms He Ting Ru –   17 To ask the Minister for Education (a) what are the Ministry’s policies and guidelines on students with gender dysphoria; (b) how often are such policies and approaches reviewed at the school and Ministry levels; (c) what level of autonomy do schools have over the setting of such policies and approaches; and (d) whether the Ministry will consider presenting a public report on these matters to Parliament on a regular basis.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MOE's focus is on the school environment and the students involved.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Schools are a common space for all students regardless of their backgrounds and circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have a duty of care to every student.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For students with gender dysphoria, our main focus is continuing to provide them with a conducive learning environment and to support their overall well-being.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Recognising that the issues are complex and that there are diverse opinions amongst students and their parents, we strive to deal with these situations sensitively and with compassion.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One particularly difficult issue is with school rules.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As each student's situation is unique, the matter must be dealt with individually.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our guiding principles are to treat these students with dignity and respect, and to provide as much support as we can to help them.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I recognise how strongly some people feel about this issue.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We welcome continued dialogue and feedback, and will strive to provide a supportive environment in schools to support our students holistically.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Issues of gender identity have become bitterly contested sources of division in the culture wars in some Western countries and societies.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We should not import these culture wars into Singapore, or allow issues of gender identity to divide our society.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ms He suggested a report to Parliament on a regular basis.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We ought to respect their requests for privacy and avoid putting out information that will compromise any student or family confidentiality.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Let us give the students and their families time and space to resolve matters amongst themselves, in consultation with their doctors and counsellors.
